footer.prototype: A research prototype for simulations with consenting participants.
error.backend: Can't reach the Ventriloquist backend. Start it with `make backend` and reload.
landing.tagline: The patient does the talking. The phone just moves its lips.
landing.lead: Ventriloquist is for someone who is awake but cannot speak, for example because of a breathing tube. A phone on the bed rail asks short yes-or-no questions, reads each answer from the patient's own movement, and says the message out loud once the patient has confirmed it.
landing.not_device_body: Ventriloquist is a research prototype, tried only in simulations with consenting participants. It does not replace clinical judgement or the nurse call system.
landing.hero_alt: A patient with a breathing tube in an ICU bed. A phone clamped to the bed rail asks “Is it about Aisyah?”; a family photo stands on the table.
landing.photo_note: AI-generated photo of a fictional patient.
landing.alone.title: When nobody is in the room
landing.alone.lead: A patient on a ventilator because of muscle weakness often cannot press the call bell, and family is not always there.
landing.alone.photo_alt: At night, a patient with a breathing tube reads “Did I say it right?” on a phone clamped to his bed rail.
landing.alone.1.title: The message reaches a person
landing.alone.1.body: It stays on the nurse's screen with a chime until someone taps “I'm coming”, and the phone says it again if nobody does. The patient hears when it has been seen.
landing.alone.2.title: It can reach family
landing.alone.2.body: For a message about a relative, the phone asks the patient before sending it on WhatsApp, then reads the reply aloud. Replies about health or bad news go to a nurse first.
landing.alone.3.title: Help from any screen
landing.alone.3.body: Giving the yes signal three times quickly raises a loud alarm on the nurse's screen, whatever the phone was doing.
landing.trail.label: Patient screen, daughter demo
landing.trail.aria: Example question trail from the daughter demo
landing.trail.q4: Is this your message: “I want to see my daughter, Aisyah.”?
landing.trail.say: I want to see my daughter, Aisyah.
landing.trail.spoken: Spoken aloud, in the first person
landing.trail.caption: A nurse had mentioned Aisyah and the patient kept looking at a family photo, so she came up first. Only the patient's answers turned the guess into a message.
landing.flip.title: Who is the ventriloquist?
landing.flip.p1: In a careless system the machine is the ventriloquist: it guesses what a patient wants and puts the words in their mouth.
landing.flip.p2: Here the patient is the ventriloquist. The phone is only the voice.
landing.flip.p3: Room context can bring a guess up sooner, but it never makes the guess true. Nothing is spoken until the patient confirms it, every message is checked afterwards with “Did I say it right?”, and the caregiver sees why each question was asked and can override any answer.
landing.demo.title: Try it without a camera
landing.demo.body: Demo sessions run in mock mode: fictional patients, no model calls, no cost. On the patient screen, answer with the keyboard: Y for yes, N for no, U for unclear, E for emergency.
landing.demo.simulated_hint: The patient answers on their own every 1.2 seconds, with an occasional mistake. Press “Start without the phone” on the caregiver screen.
landing.demo.after: Each demo opens the caregiver screen, with a QR code that opens the patient screen on a phone.
landing.how.title: How a message gets said
landing.how.1.title: Learn the patient's yes and no
landing.how.1.body: Eyebrows, a long blink, a lifted finger: whatever the patient can do. Three examples of each, recorded at the bedside.
landing.how.2.title: Ask the most useful question
landing.how.2.body: The phone ranks likely messages using the room: what the nurse said, who just visited, what the camera sees. Then it asks the question that narrows them down fastest.
landing.how.3.title: Confirm, speak, check
landing.how.3.body: When one message is very likely, the phone asks first, says it in the first person, then asks “Did I say it right?”. Unclear answers go to a caregiver.
landing.how.4.title: Spell anything else
landing.how.4.body: If the message isn't on the list, the patient spells it by letter groups, with word suggestions to save effort.
scenario.daughter.title: Mr Hasan wants to see his daughter
scenario.daughter.body: In English. A nurse mentioned Aisyah, a family photo is in view and a visitor has just left.
scenario.suction.title: Secretions after a long gap
scenario.suction.body: In Indonesian. The nurse noted noisy breathing and it has been a while since the last suction.
scenario.cold.title: Cold at night
scenario.cold.body: In English. The air conditioning is on full and the nurse said the room is freezing.
scenario.spelling.title: Something that isn't on the list
scenario.spelling.body: In Indonesian. Ibu Sri wants to know who is feeding her cat, so she spells it.
setup.title: Set up a patient
setup.lead: The profile helps Ventriloquist guess sooner: family names become possible messages, and the honorific makes Indonesian questions sound natural.
setup.name: Display name
setup.name_hint: Use a fictional name for demos, such as “Mr Hasan (fictional)”.
setup.honorific_hint: Used in Indonesian questions, for example “Apakah Bapak haus?”.
setup.family_hint: People the patient may want to see or ask about. With a WhatsApp number and their agreement, the patient can send them a message and hear their reply.
setup.family_consent: They agreed to receive the patient's messages on WhatsApp
setup.notes_hint: One per line, for example “Wears glasses”. Leave out diagnoses and medication.
setup.spiritual_hint: For example “Muslim” or “Catholic”. Lets the phone offer prayer as a message.
setup.consent: This is a simulation with a consenting participant
setup.consent_hint: Development and demos use consenting participants only, never real patients.
setup.error.name: Enter a display name.
setup.error.consent: Tick the box to confirm this is a simulation with a consenting participant.
setup.saved.title: {name} is saved
setup.saved.body: Next, teach Ventriloquist this person's yes and no. It takes about two minutes with the phone's front camera.
setup.saved.skip_hint: Skipping uses keyboard answers (mock mode) with default error rates.
cal.title: Calibrate yes and no
cal.lead: Place the phone where it will stay during sessions, facing the patient. The preview is mirrored, like a mirror.
cal.intro.1: First we check that the face and shoulders are in view and well lit.
cal.intro.2: Then 15 seconds of rest, three YES examples, three NO examples, and one practice of the emergency signal: YES three times quickly.
cal.intro.3: Each recording starts after a 3-second countdown. Clips are deleted after analysis unless you keep them for evaluation.
cal.skip_hint: Without calibration, answers come from the keyboard or from the caregiver.
cal.skip_live_hint: Without calibration, Muse Spark watches for the default signals: both eyebrows up for YES, eyes squeezed shut for NO. The caregiver can always tap the answer instead.
cal.no_camera: This browser can't use the camera here. Open this page over HTTPS on the phone, or skip calibration.
cal.camera_denied: The camera didn't start: {reason}. Allow camera access in the browser and try again.
cal.framing.title: Check the framing
cal.framing.body: Face and shoulders should fill most of the picture, with light on the face.
cal.task.rest_body: Ask the patient to rest and look at the phone. Small natural movements are fine.
cal.task.yes_body: Ask the patient to make their YES movement once, clearly.
cal.task.no_body: Ask the patient to make their NO movement once, clearly.
cal.task.emergency_body: Ask the patient to make the YES movement three times quickly. This raises the alarm during sessions.
cal.say.rest: Please rest and look at the phone.
cal.say.emergency: Please show me YES three times, quickly.
cal.no_recorder: This browser can't record video. Try Chrome on Android or Safari on iOS.
cal.mirror_note: The preview is mirrored. Describe movements by body part, never as left or right.
cal.finalize.title: Analyse the examples
cal.finalize.body: Ventriloquist describes the two movements, builds a detector for each source and measures how often it confuses them.
cal.hint: Which movement did the patient use?
cal.hint_hint: Optional. Helps the description when the movement is small.
cal.pick.title: Which movements will the patient use?
cal.pick.hint: Pick what they can do most reliably, even when tired. You will record three examples of each.
cal.mount.alt: A phone in a gooseneck clamp on the bed rail, near the face of a patient with a breathing tube.
cal.mount.title: Mount the phone
cal.mount.body: Clamp it to the bed rail about 50 cm from the face, at eye level, so the camera sees the face and shoulders. Plug it in; a session can run for hours.
cal.mount.caption: AI-generated photo of a fictional patient.
pick.unsure: Something else, or not sure yet
pick.unsure_hint: Record the examples anyway; the movement is worked out from them.
cal.results.ok: Calibration is good. YES and NO are easy to tell apart.
cal.results.not_ok: YES and NO were hard to tell apart.
cal.results.skipped: Calibration skipped. Sessions use keyboard answers and default error rates.
cal.results.no_accuracy: No detector was trained (calibration skipped or mock mode).
cal.results.errors: Error rates used by the engine

patient.missing.title: This session isn't available
patient.missing.body: Ask a caregiver to start a new session.
patient.start_hint: Turns on the voice and keeps the screen awake.
patient.start_hint_live: Turns on the voice and the camera, and keeps the screen awake.
patient.camera_error: The camera didn't start. A caregiver can answer for you.
patient.upload_error: Your answer didn't reach us. A caregiver can enter it.
patient.mock_hint: Mock: press Y / N / U, E = emergency
patient.letter_grid: Letters. The highlighted group is the one being asked about.
patient.emergency.title: A caregiver is coming now.
patient.emergency.body: Help has been called. You are not alone.
patient.paused.title: Paused
patient.paused.body: A caregiver will continue with you shortly.
patient.caregiver.title: A caregiver will come to help.
patient.caregiver.body: You don't need to do anything right now.
patient.done.title: I'm listening when you're ready.
patient.done.body: When you want to say something else, signal to a caregiver.
patient.ack.waiting: Waiting for a caregiver to see it.
patient.ack.seen: A caregiver has seen your message and is coming.
patient.ended.title: Session ended
patient.ended.body: Thank you. A caregiver can start a new session any time.
message.retracted_label: Retracted: the patient said this was wrong
caregiver.missing.title: This session isn't running
caregiver.missing.body: The backend doesn't know this session. It may have restarted, which clears sessions held in memory. Start a new one from the home page.
connect.title: Open the patient screen on the phone
connect.body: Scan with the phone on the bed rail. The phone must be on the same network; accept the certificate warning once.
connect.qr_label: QR code for the patient screen
connect.host_hint: Use this computer's LAN address, or a tunnel hostname.
now.title: Now
now.not_started: Waiting for the patient screen. Tap “Tap to start” on the phone, or start from here.
now.done: Message finished. Start a new one when the patient signals.
now.paused: Paused. Resume when the patient is ready.
now.answer_for: Answer for the patient (shown with an override badge)
bars.title: Likely messages
bars.empty: Guesses appear once the session starts.
bars.bounded.cap: Context alone can't push one guess above the cap.
bars.bounded.floor: Kept above the floor so it can still come back.
bars.bounded.other_min: “Something else” never drops below its minimum.
bars.bounded.generic: Limited by a safety bound on the prior.
bars.personal_hint: Adjusted by what this patient said in earlier sessions.
bars.chip_missing: This evidence is no longer in the current context.
bars.legend.chips: Tap a chip to see its evidence.
trail.title: Question trail
trail.override_hint: A caregiver entered this answer for the patient.
messages.title: Messages from the patient
pending.title: Messages waiting for a caregiver
pending.escalated: Nobody has acknowledged this yet. Please go to the bed.
relay.title: Family messages
relay.approve_title: Send to {name} ({relation}) on WhatsApp? The patient said yes.
relay.simulated: Simulated relative: no WhatsApp account is connected, nothing leaves this computer.
relay.whatsapp: From the hospital's WhatsApp number to {phone}, as the approved message template.
relay.review_title: {name} replied. Please read it before the patient hears it.
relay.empty: Nothing sent to family yet. When the patient asks for a relative who agreed to receive messages, the phone offers to send it.
context.title: Room context
context.empty: No scene facts, events or memories yet.
transcript.title: Live transcript
transcript.empty: Nothing said in the room in the last 15 minutes.
transcript.mock_hint: Mock mode: type what was said in the room.
transcript.live_hint: Type a line, or upload room audio to transcribe.
transcript.speaker: Speaker
transcript.placeholder: Your son Rizal called, he's coming tonight.
event.title: Log what just happened
event.hint: Events shape the next guesses. “Medication given” records only that it happened: never enter drug names, doses or diagnoses.
overlay.title: Latest clip
overlay.empty: No clip yet. In mock mode answers come from the keyboard, so there is nothing to track.
overlay.empty_live: No clip yet. After the first answer, the tracked body part is drawn here, from boxes only.
overlay.caption: {provider} tracking “{prompt}”, {n} frames. Only boxes are kept, never the video.
calls.title: Recent model calls
alarm.title: The patient needs help now.
alarm.body: {name} gave the emergency signal. Go to the bedside.
sensitive.title: Verify in person with the patient
sensitive.body: The patient spelled something that may be sensitive. It has not been spoken. Check with the patient in person before deciding.
reason.title: A caregiver is needed
reason.question_cap: Ten questions reached. Please help the patient in person.
reason.unclear: Responses are unclear. Please check with the patient in person.
reason.inconsistent: Answers contradicted each other. Please check with the patient in person.
reason.tap_answer: The answer was unclear twice. Tap the patient's answer above.
reason.no_match: The message didn't match the list. Help in person or start spelling.
reason.no_questions_left: No more useful questions. Help in person or start spelling.
reason.spelling_stuck: Spelling is stuck. Please help the patient in person.
reason.internal_error: Something went wrong in the backend. Continue with the patient in person.
budget.title: Model spend against the budget cap
budget.mock_notice: Budget guard switched to mock: {spent} of {max} spent. Answers now come from the keyboard or the caregiver.
memory.title: Memory
memory.lead: What Ventriloquist remembers about this patient across sessions. Every entry shows where it came from, and nothing is added without a caregiver's approval.
memory.ops.title: Proposed changes
memory.ops.hint: The curator reads confirmed messages and the room transcript, then proposes changes that cite their sources.
memory.entries.title: Remembered
memory.entries.empty: Nothing remembered yet. Add a fact or approve a proposal.
memory.form.title: Add a caregiver fact
memory.form.hint: Habits and preferences, such as “Likes the blinds half open”. Clinical or sensitive facts are refused.
memory.curve.title: Learning curve
memory.curve.hint: Mean questions per confirmed message, per session. Lower means the phone is learning this patient.
memory.curve.empty: The curve appears after the first confirmed message.
chart.table: Show the numbers as a table
eval.title: Simulation
eval.label: Simulation, not clinical evidence
eval.lead: Simulated patients with a known message answer yes or no with a chosen error rate. We count the questions each strategy needs and how often it ends with the right message.
eval.saved_source: Saved run: {n} trials per cell, seed {seed}.
eval.how.title: How to read this
eval.how.body: The fixed-order board walks the same categories every time, like a laminated card. The best-question strategies pick the question with the highest expected information gain; with context, room evidence shapes the starting guesses within safety bounds.
eval.detector.title: Detector accuracy
eval.detector.body: How well the camera reads yes and no is measured separately, on labelled clips recorded with consenting participants. Run the script below to print confusion matrices per source.
settings.title: Settings
settings.lead: These apply to new sessions. Mode and privacy changes need the passcode when one is set.
settings.mode.title: Mode
settings.mode.legend: Where answers and room context are analysed
settings.mode.mock_hint: No model calls and no cost. Answers come from the keyboard, a simulated patient or the caregiver.
settings.mode.live_hint: The camera reads answers and the room is analysed by Meta's models.
settings.mode.live_warning: Live mode sends clips to Meta's API and spends real credit on every question.
settings.privacy_hint: Use open-weight models under a zero-data-retention policy instead of Meta's API.
settings.passcode_hint: Required to leave mock mode or turn on privacy mode.
unlock.title: Live mode on this device
unlock.hint: This is a public deployment. Everyone gets mock mode, which costs nothing. With the passcode, this browser uses Meta's models: the camera reads answers and the room is analysed.
unlock.done: Live mode is unlocked on this device.
settings.leaves.title: What leaves this device
settings.leaves.mock: Nothing. No clips, snapshots or audio leave the computer running Ventriloquist.
settings.leaves.live: Answer clips, room snapshots and room audio go to Meta's API with store=false, so they are not kept.
settings.leaves.privacy: Clips, snapshots and audio go to Muse Spark Open on Baseten under its zero-data-retention policy. SAM runs self-hosted, or the phone falls back to an on-device motion tracker.
settings.tau: Confirm when the top message reaches
settings.tau_hint: Lower asks to confirm sooner but risks more “No, that's not it”. The message is only spoken after the patient says yes.
settings.window_hint: How long the camera records after each question.
settings.language_hint: Each patient's own language still wins on the patient screen.
settings.budget_cap_hint: At 70% the console warns; at 90% the guard switches to mock.
settings.flag.use_sam_hint: Tracks the calibrated body part in each clip.
settings.flag.use_spark_judge_hint: A second opinion that watches each clip.
settings.flag.use_transcribe_hint: Turns room audio into transcript evidence.
settings.flag.use_wonder_hint: Proposes memory changes after each session, for approval.
settings.flag.idle_watch_hint: Watches between messages for a YES (new message) or the emergency signal.
settings.keep_clips_hint: Off by default: clips are deleted right after they are analysed.

demo.notice.title: Hosted demo: everything runs in your browser
demo.notice.body: The real engine, written in Python, runs here through WebAssembly (Pyodide), in mock mode: no camera, no server, no API keys. Answer with the Y and N keys, or tick "Simulated patient" and watch. The first start downloads about 20 MB and takes a few seconds.
demo.stage.error: The engine could not load. Check your connection and reload.
demo.connect_note: In the hosted demo the patient phone is shown on the right. Run Ventriloquist locally to open it on a real phone.
demo.phone_hint: Click the phone, then answer with Y and N (U = unclear, E = emergency).
transcript.mic_hint: Sends 8-second audio chunks to the transcriber while on. Turn it on only with everyone's agreement. What the phone itself says is filtered out.
